doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Family reaction to the band
summary: His wife was supportive and his daughter Lisa enjoyed Helen Humes and Laurel Watson, though vacations were with the band.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What did your wife and daughter think of this passion of yours?

I think my wife was very supportive. I think she enjoyed meeting all these people. My daughter liked it, it wasn’t her kind of music but I remember once when Helen Humes sang in our house she was knocked over by Helen Humes’ singing. And she liked Laurel Watson, because Lisa wanted to sing and Laurel gave her some pointers. And so she kind of, I think they liked, or they respected what I was doing. And they enjoyed it. They enjoyed it I think.
Well it must be rewarding and then difficult at the same time.
It was difficult for my wife because I would go away with the band sometimes and I remember Lisa saying once, my daughter, “why do we always have to go on a vacation with the band?”
But also the fact that you’re getting these people in the band and then eventually many of them pass away.
That’s a big emotional investment on your part.
